newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says no BOE gold loan, arms deal on cards.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says no BOE gold loan, arms deal on cards.

text.p: South African authorities on Tuesday denied reports the country was negotiating a gold-for-arms deal with the Bank of England.

Officials at the departments of Finance and Foreign Affairs and Armscor, the South African government's weapons procurement agency, said the mooted deal, reported by South African newspapers last week, was not on the agenda.
"We have not been approached on this at the department. It's not something we know anything about," said Foreign Affairs spokesman Pieter Swanepoel.
"The Department of Finance has not been approached on this idea," said spokeswoman Jennifer Wilson.
South African Reserve Bank deputy governor James Cross also said the central bank was not in discussions with the Bank of England regarding gold sales.

Friday's Business Day newspaper said a British defence industry consortium had proposed a gold-based arms deal with South Africa worth over 10 billion rand including submarines, fighter jets, tanks and light frigates.

"The British financing model is understood to involve the purchase by a London export bank of gold from the Bank of England or some other holder of significant stocks of gold for sale on the world market. The sale would generate the capital for the SA arms acquisitions over several years," the paper said.
The Reserve Bank's Cross noted it would not be cheaper for the government to fund offshore purchases via a gold loan than any other mechanism.

Armscor spokesman Billy Nell said the agency was looking for "creative" packages to finance a South African weapons upgrade in the face of severe budget cuts, but these were mainly based on counter-trade or so-called industrial participation packages.
"Industrial participation is becoming more and more important by the day," he said.
Financing of this upgrade would be a sophisticated decision to be taken at cabinet level, he added.
